outroLine: How many did you get? Thirty or more and you'd pass! Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Welcome back, quiz friends! Today: real questions from the U.S. citizenship test. To pass, you need about sixty percent. So, can you get thirty out of fifty? Grab a pen. First one: what is the capital of the United States?
lines.a: Washington, D C! New York was the first capital, under Washington himself.

lines.q: How many stars are on the U.S. flag?
lines.a: Fifty! One for every state. The last two were added in nineteen sixty.

lines.q: And how many stripes are on the flag?
lines.a: Thirteen! For the thirteen original colonies.

lines.q: What do Americans celebrate on the Fourth of July?
lines.a: Independence Day! The Declaration was adopted on July fourth, seventeen seventy-six.

lines.q: Which ocean is on the West Coast of the United States?
lines.a: The Pacific! The Atlantic is on the East Coast.

lines.q: What is the name of the national anthem?
lines.a: The Star-Spangled Banner! It only became official in nineteen thirty-one.

lines.q: Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
lines.a: American Indians, or Native Americans! For thousands of years.

lines.q: Which of these is a U.S. territory, not a state?
lines.a: Puerto Rico! Hawaii and Alaska are states, and Bermuda is British.

lines.q: The United States declared independence from which country?
lines.a: Great Britain! In seventeen seventy-six.

lines.q: Which of these rights is in the First Amendment?
lines.a: Freedom of speech! Ten easy ones done. How many so far?

lines.q: Round two, a bit harder. Who was President during the Civil War?
lines.a: Abraham Lincoln! Grant became President later, in eighteen sixty-nine.

lines.q: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
lines.a: Thomas Jefferson! He was only thirty-three.

lines.q: What are the first ten amendments to the Constitution called?
lines.a: The Bill of Rights! Ratified in seventeen ninety-one.

lines.q: How many years is one term for a U.S. senator?
lines.a: Six years! The longest term in Congress.

lines.q: How many years is one presidential term?
lines.a: Four years! And a President can be elected only twice.

lines.q: Who is the Commander in Chief of the military?
lines.a: The President! A civilian always leads the military.

lines.q: Who makes federal laws?
lines.a: Congress! The Senate and the House together.

lines.q: How many justices sit on the Supreme Court?
lines.a: Nine! It's been nine since eighteen sixty-nine.

lines.q: In which year was the Constitution written?
lines.a: Seventeen eighty-seven! Seventeen seventy-six was the Declaration. Sneaky one.

lines.q: Who did the United States fight in World War Two?
lines.a: Japan, Germany and Italy! Twenty done. You're halfway through the easy part.

lines.q: Welcome to the hard round! Who was the first Postmaster General of the United States?
lines.a: Benjamin Franklin! He also ran a newspaper and invented bifocals.

lines.q: What territory did the United States buy from France in eighteen-oh-three?
lines.a: The Louisiana Territory! It doubled the size of the country.

lines.q: Who was President during World War One?
lines.a: Woodrow Wilson! He later won the Nobel Peace Prize.

lines.q: Who was President during the Great Depression and World War Two?
lines.a: Franklin Roosevelt! The only President elected four times.

lines.q: What is the minimum age to vote in federal elections?
lines.a: Eighteen! If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: How old must a President be, at least?
lines.a: Thirty-five! The youngest ever was Teddy Roosevelt, at forty-two.

lines.q: How many years is one term in the House of Representatives?
lines.a: Two years! So they're always campaigning.

lines.q: Susan B. Anthony is famous for fighting for what?
lines.a: Women's rights! She was even arrested for voting in eighteen seventy-two.

lines.q: What did the Emancipation Proclamation do?
lines.a: It freed the slaves in the Confederate states! Signed by Lincoln in eighteen sixty-three.

lines.q: The Federalist Papers argued in favour of what?
lines.a: Passing the U.S. Constitution! Eighty-five essays in New York newspapers.

lines.q: Now the very hard round. Which of these men co-wrote the Federalist Papers?
lines.a: James Madison! With Alexander Hamilton and John Jay. Jefferson was in France.

lines.q: Which of these is not a branch of the U.S. government?
lines.a: The military! The three branches are legislative, executive and judicial.

lines.q: Men must register for Selective Service between which ages?
lines.a: Between eighteen and twenty-six! Most people get this one wrong.

lines.q: What is usually the last day to send in federal income tax forms?
lines.a: April fifteenth! Tax day.

lines.q: If both the President and the Vice President can no longer serve, who becomes President?
lines.a: The Speaker of the House! Then the President pro tempore of the Senate.

lines.q: Under the Constitution, which of these powers belongs to the states?
lines.a: Providing schooling and education! Printing money and declaring war are federal.

lines.q: What was the main concern of the United States during the Cold War?
lines.a: Communism! It lasted from the late nineteen forties to nineteen ninety-one.

lines.q: Life, liberty and the pursuit of what?
lines.a: Happiness! The philosopher John Locke had written property. Jefferson changed it.

lines.q: Which of these was one of the original thirteen states?
lines.a: Georgia! Vermont joined in seventeen ninety-one and Maine in eighteen twenty.

lines.q: The Constitution begins with which three words?
lines.a: We the People! Four score and seven years ago is Lincoln's Gettysburg Address.

lines.q: Welcome to the legend round! In which month do Americans vote for President?
lines.a: November! On the Tuesday after the first Monday.

lines.q: Who wrote the words of The Star-Spangled Banner?
lines.a: Francis Scott Key! He watched a battle at Fort McHenry in eighteen fourteen.

lines.q: Which document did the Constitution replace?
lines.a: The Articles of Confederation! The first plan for the government was too weak.

lines.q: Which amendment gave women the right to vote?
lines.a: The nineteenth! In nineteen twenty.

lines.q: Which amendment lowered the voting age to eighteen?
lines.a: The twenty-sixth! In nineteen seventy-one, during the Vietnam War.

lines.q: Which amendment ended slavery?
lines.a: The thirteenth! In eighteen sixty-five.

lines.q: Who was President during the Louisiana Purchase?
lines.a: Thomas Jefferson! He paid about three cents an acre.

lines.q: Who was the first Secretary of the Treasury?
lines.a: Alexander Hamilton! Yes, the one from the musical. Two left, stay with me!

lines.q: From which country did the United States buy Alaska?
lines.a: Russia! In eighteen sixty-seven, for about two cents an acre.

lines.q: Last one. Which state was the first to approve the Constitution?
lines.a: Delaware! That's why it's called the First State.
